cards.text: The LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader, on Mount Sinai and gives him a message for the Israelites. It covers what they're to do once they enter the land He's giving them. And it starts with a Sabbath.

cards.question: When Israel enters the land, the LORD says the ___ itself must observe a Sabbath to Him.

cards.text: For six years they sow, prune and gather, but year seven is a Sabbath of complete rest for the land. The fields get a whole year OFF, friend, and my mixer has never had a day off in its life.

cards.question: True or false: In the Sabbath year, the farmers can still reap the aftergrowth and gather grapes from the untended vines.
Whatever the land yields on its own during the Sabbath year becomes food. Who gets to eat it?

answers.text: The household and even the wild animals
The widows and orphans of the town

cards.text: Then God has them count seven Sabbaths of years, forty-nine years in all. Then a horn sounds throughout the land on the tenth day of the seventh month, the Day of Atonement.

cards.question: After seven Sabbaths of years, the horn sounds. Which year does God tell Israel to set apart as holy?

cards.text: The fiftieth year is the Jubilee, when liberty is proclaimed in the land for all its inhabitants. Every time my old junk drawer slid open, all of us in there held our breath hoping for a day like THIS.

cards.question: In the Year of Jubilee, each person is to return to his ___ and to his clan.
The land already rests every seventh year. True or false: In the Jubilee year, God tells Israel not to sow the land or harvest the untended vines.

cards.text: The Jubilee is holy to them. During it, they may eat only the crops taken directly from the field.
Since land goes back home at the Jubilee, a buyer is really paying for the harvests left until then. And God's rule for buyers and sellers is simple: don't take advantage of each other.

cards.question: More years left before the Jubilee means a ___ price. Fewer years left means a ___ price.

cards.text: Then God says that line again: don't take advantage of each other, but fear your God. Friend, somebody once bought me out of a bin for 25 cents, and honestly, they OVERPAID.

cards.question: God tells Israel to keep His statutes and carefully observe His judgments. What does He say comes of it?

answers.text: They will dwell securely in the land
They will rule over the nations nearby
Their enemies will make peace with them

cards.text: Then God says out loud what they might be wondering: "What will we eat in the seventh year if we do not sow or gather our produce?" Fair question, friend.

cards.question: God says He'll send His blessing on Israel in the sixth year. What does the land do that year?

answers.text: Yields a crop for three years
Yields only enough for one year

cards.text: That one blessed crop feeds them while they sow in the eighth year, all the way until the ninth year's harvest comes in. That's like baking ONE batch and pulling three trays out of the oven.
Now God gets to the heart of it. The land must not be sold permanently.

cards.question: Why can't land in Israel be sold for good?

answers.text: Because the land belongs to the LORD
Because the land belongs to the priests
Because the land belongs to the king

cards.text: Israel lives on the land as foreigners and residents with the LORD, so every property needs a way to be bought back. Friend, I lived in the Millers' junk drawer for years, and I never once owned that drawer.

cards.question: Say an Israelite falls on hard times and sells some of his property. Who can step in and buy it back for him?

cards.text: But what if the man who sold his land has no one to buy it back? If he prospers later and has enough, he can buy it back himself.

cards.question: To buy his land back, the man counts the ___ since its sale and repays the balance to the buyer.
True or false: If the man never gets enough to buy his land back, it stays with the buyer forever.

cards.text: Then a few special cases. A house in a walled city can be bought back within one full year, and if it isn't, it's the buyer's for good. But village houses and Levite houses go back in the Jubilee, and the Levites' pastureland can't be sold at all.
Now God turns from land to people, starting with a countryman who becomes destitute and can't support himself.

cards.question: God tells Israel to help a destitute countryman as they would a ___ or stranger, so he can keep living among them.
What does God say not to take from a destitute countryman?

cards.text: No lending a poor countryman silver at interest, and no selling him food for profit. That's like handing a friend a cookie and then sending him a BILL for the crumbs.
God reminds them He is the LORD their God, the One giving them the land of Canaan. Then He gives a law for a countryman who gets so destitute that he sells himself to a fellow Israelite.

cards.question: Say an Israelite becomes destitute and sells himself to a fellow Israelite. How must the buyer treat him?

answers.text: As a hired worker and not a slave
As a slave for the rest of his life
As a prisoner until he pays up

cards.question: True or false: An Israelite who sells himself to a fellow Israelite goes free with his children in the Year of Jubilee.
Why does God say the Israelites must not be sold as slaves?

answers.text: They're His servants He brought out of Egypt
There are too few of them to spare
Their fathers made a vow at Sinai

cards.text: God says their menservants and maidservants may be bought from the nations around them and from foreigners living among them. Those may become property, be left to their sons and be made slaves for life.

cards.question: True or false: Under these rules, an Israelite may rule harshly over his fellow Israelite.

cards.text: Now flip it around. A foreigner living among them prospers, and a poor Israelite nearby sells himself to that foreigner.

cards.question: An Israelite who sells himself to a foreigner can still be ___ back by an uncle, a cousin or any close relative.

cards.text: He can even buy himself back if he prospers, and the price is figured from the years left until the Jubilee, at a hired hand's daily wages. Careful math, friend, and I lose count of my chocolate chips at ELEVEN.
Until then, he's treated like a man hired from year to year. And his foreign owner must not rule over him harshly in Israel's sight.

cards.question: True or false: If an Israelite who sold himself to a foreigner is never bought back, he stays with that owner for life.

cards.text: God says it twice: the Israelites are His servants, whom He brought out of Egypt, and He closes with "I am the LORD your God." Keep that apron on, friend, because this teaching isn't done yet.
